decision_brief.headline: The FedWatch dark spot persists — third straight snapshot — and both boards sit just above policy: the October Fed average 1.5 bp above the range midpoint, CORRA futures 12.5 bp above target. What changed is the data: JOLTS showed openings down 256k and Canada's July GDP landed flat, so the cooling is real but gradual, and the next repricing candidates are today's GDP/PCE prints and Friday's payrolls, not either decision.
decision_brief.summary: Both central banks remain on hold — Fed 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28, BoC 2.25% into Oct 28 — and nothing verifiable is dislocated against policy: ZQV26, the October 30-day Fed funds contract, closed 96.110 on Sep 29, implying a 3.890% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR, 1.5 bp above the 3.875% range midpoint; CRAU26's quote side (mid 97.625) implies roughly 2.375% quarterly average CORRA, 12.5 bp above target. Neither is a meeting probability and CME FedWatch returned HTTP 403 a third day running, so no single-meeting distribution exists anywhere in this snapshot. The margin of change since yesterday is in releases, not prices: August JOLTS openings fell 256k to 7.079M (new weight-0.5 dovish card), Canada's July GDP by industry came in at 0.0% — essentially unchanged, so the second-consecutive-contraction falsifier did not trigger — and Tuesday's tape was mildly risk-off (SPY -0.18%, TLT -0.50%, ZEB 0.81% lower) while gold bounced +1.32%. The rates are patient; the data keeps cooling in small steps.

largest_pnl_risks: Front-end shorts into Oct 28: with no verifiable meeting distribution, a position sized off ZQV26's 3.890% is an October monthly-average exposure whose average mostly predates the decision — it can reprice on December without the Fed moving.

Today's double release (Q2 GDP third estimate plus August PCE at 08:30 ET) is the cheapest way to get hurt on a hold-sized front-end position this week; Oct 2 payrolls lands six business days before the FOMC.
The JOLTS cooling is one release from a low base: a rebound in the next JOLTS print unwinds the dovish increment with no Fed action at all.
The BoC hawkish column is empty by absence, not by evidence: an upward retail revision removes the dovish lean with no new data arriving.
This frame expires: both decisions land within four weeks, and by mid-October the missing pricing becomes a view on the data itself.

fed.stance: Hold at 3.75-4.00% — no verifiable meeting edge
fed.rationale: The Sep 16 FOMC raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%; that completed action is not itself an October surprise. FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot and none is estimated. ZQV26 closed 96.110 on Sep 29, implying a 3.890% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR — 1.5 bp above the 3.875% midpoint — but its average is set almost entirely before the Oct 28 decision, so it prices the pre-decision regime, not the meeting. The new JOLTS card adds cooling evidence (openings -256k); Michigan's final 48.1 beat consensus yet was the lowest reading in four months.

boc.stance: Hold at 2.25% — consumer soft, hawkish column empty by absence
boc.rationale: The Sep 2 decision held the overnight target at 2.25%, with the next decision Oct 28 alongside the MPR. With no weighted hawkish card, the Canadian rope reads dovish by absence rather than on positive evidence; July retail (-0.7% headline, -1.1% volume) and July GDP by industry (0.0%, essentially unchanged) keep the growth picture flat-to-soft. CRAU26's quote side (mid 97.625) implies roughly 2.375% quarterly average CORRA, 12.5 bp above target, but it spans the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions and cannot be decomposed into either.

reconsider_if: CRAU26's quote side implying more than 2.50% average CORRA (a further 12.5 bp above the current ~2.375%) against the 2.25% policy target.
Canada's September LFS on Oct 9 showing a second consecutive large employment decline would justify an outright dovish view.
An upward retail revision would remove the dovish lean with no new data arriving — the hawkish column is empty by construction.
A decomposition of the quarterly CORRA contract into meeting-dated legs would make the October decision tradeable.

decision_brief.trade_status_rationale: Deliberate abstention, not an absent view. Neither board has a verifiable single-meeting distribution (FedWatch 403 for a third day) and the verifiable contracts sit just off policy — the October Fed average 1.5 bp above the range midpoint, CORRA futures 12.5 bp above target — so there is no dislocated price to trade against; the asymmetry worth watching is the cooling data (JOLTS -256k), not the policy rate. This frame is wrong by 2026-10-09, when both the October preliminary Michigan and the September LFS print.

price_thresholds.meaning: The band that maps to the current 3.75-4.00% target range. Outside it the contract's dominant period prices a move; it is not a single-meeting probability.
